items.summary: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals denied John Diego Rodriguez-Lage's petition for review of a final order of removal. The court affirmed the Board of Immigration Appeals' finding that the petitioner did not establish the statutory criteria for severe spousal mistreatment required for VAWA cancellation and dismissed other claims as unreviewable. The court further confirmed its jurisdiction to review agency applications of the statutory severe mistreatment standard, abrogating prior circuit precedent on that point.

items.summary: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals dismissed in part and denied in part a petition for review filed by Keidy Dallana Posada-Arriola and her children, seeking to reopen removal proceedings. The court affirmed the Board of Immigration Appeals' denial of the motion, finding it lacked jurisdiction to review the denial of sua sponte reopening as no incorrect legal premise or arbitrary departure from settled adjudication was present. The court also rejected the petitioners' due process claims.

items.summary: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the District Court's dismissal of Antonio K. Witherspoon's civil rights complaint against a New Jersey State Judge. The complaint alleged the judge violated his constitutional rights by denying a suppression motion in a state court case. The court found the judge was entitled to absolute judicial immunity for the described judicial acts and that the criminal statutes invoked did not provide a private right of action.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a district court's dismissal of a case for lack of personal jurisdiction. The appeals court determined that the defendants had sufficient minimum contacts with Colorado due to the nature of the alleged transactions and the acceptance of a position governed by Colorado law.

items.summary: The United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit affirmed a district court's grant of summary judgment in favor of Nissan North America, Inc., and Nissan Motor Acceptance Corporation. Plaintiff Matthew Stewart had alleged age discrimination under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act regarding his unsuccessful application for a new position (P5) after a company reorganization. items.summary: The United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit affirmed the district court's judgment in a patent infringement case between DS Advanced Enterprises, Ltd. and Lowe's Home Centers, LLC. The court upheld the summary judgment of non-infringement, finding the accused product lacked a "metal housing" as claimed in U.S. Patent No. 11,054,118. It also affirmed the denial of DS Advanced's motion to alter the judgment, the sanctions against DS Advanced's attorney for violating a protective order, and the denial of Lowe's motion for attorneys' fees.

items.summary: The Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of Christopher H. items.summary: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), through Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), is incorporating by reference a collection of production measurement industry standards and safety industry standards into its regulations governing oil, gas, and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS). Incorporation of these documents by reference will provide industry with up-to-date, minimum requirements for measuring oil and gas production volumes and enhancing safety. Compliance with these standards will reduce uncertainty in the measurement of oil and gas production and update the minimum standards in the safety regulations.
items.title: Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf—Documents Incorporated by Reference

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-7232; Project Identifier AD-2026-00784-E; Amendment 39-23516; AD 2026-22-14] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. En
items.summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2018-26-01 for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. AD 2018-26-01 required initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. Since the FAA issued AD 2018-26-01, CFM issued updated service material providing improvements to the ultrasonic inspection procedures and expanding the inspection area. This AD requires initial and repetitive ultrasonic inspections or eddy current inspections of certain fan blades for crack indications and, depending on the results of the inspections, replacement with parts eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Model H160-B helicopters. This AD was prompted by a determination that a gap without fire-resistant sealant (sealant) may be present in the cargo bay near the fuel segregation box. This AD requires inspecting for any missing sealant and, depending on findings, corrective action. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13831; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00809-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters AGEN
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-08-51, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model MBB-BK 117 D-3 helicopters. AD 2026-08-51 requires inspecting the rotor hub-shaft for cracks, replacing any rotor hub-shaft that has any crack, and reporting information after accomplishment of the replacement. AD 2026-08-51 also prohibits installing any affected rotor hub-shaft on any helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-08-51, it was determined that additional repetitive inspections (including eddy current inspections) are necessary, and that revising the compliance time to account for hoist operations is necessary. This proposed AD would retain the actions of AD 2026-08-51 and would require additional repetitive inspections. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters

items.summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bell Textron Canada Limited (Bell) Model 429 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of premature wear-out of certain spherical bearings due to a quality escape of the spherical bearing monoballs not receiving the required hard coating. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the tail rotor (TR) pitch link assemblies and their bearings for cracks, wear, and mechanical or corrosion damage and, depending on the results, replacing any affected TR pitch link assembly. This AD also allows an affected part to be installed in a helicopter if certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Bell Textron Canada Limited Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-8790; Project Identifier MCAI-2025-01793-R; Amendment 39-23523; AD 2026-23-06] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters AGENC
items.summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-08-06 which applied to certain Airbus Helicopters Model SA330J helicopters. AD 2025-08-06 required repetitively inspecting for a gap between the main gearbox (MGB) oil cooling fan assembly rotor blade and the upper section of the guide vane bearing housing, replacing the MGB fan rotor bearings with serviceable bearings if necessary, and at a later compliance time replacing the MGB fan rotor bearing assembly with an improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, which constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections. Since AD 2025-08-06 was issued, the FAA determined that the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly should be extended. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-08-06 and increases the compliance time for installing the improved MGB fan rotor bearing assembly. This AD also prohibits installing any MGB fan rotor bearings and any MGB fan rotor bearing assembly, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13832; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00623-R] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administration
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-10-10, which applies to all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N, SA 365 N1, AS 365 N2, and AS 365 N3 helicopters. AD 2024-10-10 requires a one-time inspection for proper positioning of the tail rotor (TR) actuator harness and cable tie installation and, depending on the results, corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-10-10, the manufacturer developed a modification to reroute the yaw harness that would apply to certain model helicopters. This proposed AD would retain some of the actions of AD 2024-10-10 and would also require, for certain model helicopters, modifying the helicopter. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters

items.summary: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) is revising its regulations addressing the circumstances under which a request for rehearing is denied absent Commission action within a particular time frame. Currently, the Commission's regulations provide that unless the Commission acts upon a request for rehearing within 30 days after the request is filed, the request is denied. As revised in this final rule, the regulation will apply only to matters subject to the rehearing and judicial review provisions in the Federal Power Act (FPA) and Natural Gas Act (NGA).

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS 38 CFR Part 77 [Docket No. VA-2026-VHA-0496] RIN 2900-AS64 Streamlining the Application Process for Grants for Adaptive Sports Programs for Disabled Veterans and Disabled Members of the Armed Forces AGENCY: De
items.summary: This proposed rule would amend the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations that govern grants for adaptive sports programs for disabled veterans and disabled members of the armed forces to allow for a more efficient review and selection of applicants for the grant. This rule would ensure that the grant aligns with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards by requiring applicants to submit an application within the VA established deadline for submission; requiring that all adaptive sports grants be openly competed; and adding a new section on appropriate actions VA may take to enforce this part. The changes proposed by this rulemaking will improve program administration without negatively impacting the veteran athletes supported by these grants.
items.title: Streamlining the Application Process for Grants for Adaptive Sports Programs for Disabled Veterans and Disabled Members of the Armed Forces

items.summary: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-21-08, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, -800, and -900ER series airplanes. AD 2026-21-08 required a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side form-in-place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on-condition actions. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-21-08, the FAA has determined that the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of AD 2026-21-08 omits reference to a certain date. This AD retains all of the requirements of AD 2026-21-08 and adds the omitted reference to the compliance time exception specified in paragraph (h) of this AD. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF LABOR Employee Benefits Security Administration 29 CFR Part 2550 RIN 1210-AC37 Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights AGENCY: Employee Benefits Security Administr
items.summary: In this proposed rule, the Department of Labor (Department) clarifies the fiduciary duty of loyalty under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA). The proposed rule affirms that ERISA's duty of loyalty requires fiduciaries to act with the exclusive purpose of ensuring retirement security and providing promised benefits to plan participants and their beneficiaries. The amendments clarify the neutral application of ERISA's fiduciary duties of prudence and loyalty to selecting investments and investment courses of action, and to exercising shareholder rights, including proxy voting, the use of written proxy voting policies and guidelines, and shareholder engagement activities. The amendments would enhance the regulation by adding an affirmative expression of the duty of loyalty that is more consistent with the statute, and removing the tiebreaker test and participant preference provisions, which do not comport with the best reading of the statute and are susceptible to abuse, including use by a fiduciary as pretext to employ plan assets to pursue personal preferences or objectives unrelated to financial benefits under the plan. [official summary truncated; see source]
items.title: Loyalty and the Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights

items.summary: This action amends Class D and Class E airspace over Tri-Cities, TN. Specifically, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class D and Class E surface area airspace by expanding the radius and lateral boundaries to the northeast and removing the Tri-Cities Class E surface area extension airspace to the northeast. Additionally, this action modifies the Tri-Cities Class E transitional airspace beginning at 700 feet above the surface by expanding the lateral boundaries of the western portion of the airspace. Lastly, this action updates the airport name within the Class D and E legal descriptions and other outdated verbiage.
items.title: Amendment of Class D Airspace and Class E Airspace Over Tri-Cities, TN

items.opening_verbatim: SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION 17 CFR Parts 240 and 242 [Release No. 34-106950; File No. S7-2026-40] RIN 3235-AN54 Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail AGENCY: Securities and Exchange Commission
items.summary: Although the consolidated audit trail (the “CAT”) continues to be a necessary regulatory tool, its decentralized governance has presented certain challenges to administering the CAT. To address those shortcomings, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission” or the “SEC”) proposes to assume direct control of the CAT. Specifically, the Commission is proposing amendments to Regulation NMS under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act”) that would rescind Rule 613, which obligates the national securities exchanges and national securities associations (collectively, the “SROs”) to act jointly to develop a national market system plan to develop, implement, and maintain the CAT (the “CAT NMS Plan”). The Commission is simultaneously proposing new Rule 17a-26, which would require the SROs and broker-dealers to record and electronically report to a central repository substantially the same information that was previously required to be recorded and reported pursuant to Rule 613, the CAT NMS Plan, related SRO compliance rules, and related exemptive relief previously issued by the Commission.
items.title: Restructuring the Governance and Funding Model of the Consolidated Audit Trail

items.summary: H.R. 2478, the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025, amends Section 22 of the Investment Company Act of 1940. Registered open-end investment companies and transfer agents that elect to comply may request contact information for an adult individual for non-institutional direct at-fund accounts, and may postpone redemption payments for more than seven days for up to 15 business days, extendable by 10 business days, when they reasonably believe financial exploitation of a specified adult has occurred, is occurring, or was attempted. The Act also directs the Securities and Exchange Commission to submit a report with regulatory and legislative recommendations to Congress within one year of enactment.

items.summary: H.R. 9640, the Earth MRI Reauthorization Act of 2026, amends Section 40201 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to add modern sensing and data-driven methods to the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative and to include the U.S. Geological Survey's 3D Hydrography Program among integrated data sources. The bill authorizes $84,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 and directs the USGS Director to give preference, to the extent practicable, to United States-owned and United States-controlled contractors. It also requires entities contracting with the USGS under the Initiative to disclose the ownership of the primary contractor and each subcontractor. The bill passed the House on November 18, 2026, and was placed on the Senate calendar on November 19, 2026.

items.summary: H.R. 973, the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, directs the Consumer Product Safety Commission to promulgate, within 180 days of enactment, ANSI/CAN/UL 2271, ANSI/CAN/UL 2849, and ANSI/CAN/UL 2272 as consumer product safety standards, limited to consumer products as defined in the Consumer Product Safety Act. The Act treats revisions to these voluntary standards as Commission standards effective 180 days after the standards organization notifies the Commission, unless the Commission determines within 90 days that the revision does not improve safety. The Commission must also report to Congress within five years of enactment on fires, explosions, and other hazards involving lithium-ion batteries in micromobility products.
items.title: HR 973 ENR: Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act

As reflected in the visible portion of the text, the bill directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to establish an assessment program for commercial-scale offshore aquaculture through demonstration projects, establishes an Office of Aquaculture within the National Marine Fisheries Service, and addresses permits, Aquaculture Centers of Excellence, workforce development, and working waterfronts. items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 726 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 2883 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES September 18 (legislative day, September 16), 2025 Mr. Whitehouse (for himself, Mr. Scott of South Carolina , and Ms. Blunt Rochester ) introduced the
items.summary: S. 2883, the Quantifying Uncertainty and Action to Help Optimize Growth of Shellfish Act of 2025 or QUAHOGS Act of 2025, was introduced by Senator Whitehouse and reported by Senator Cruz with an amendment on November 20, 2026. The bill directs the Secretary of Commerce to convene an East Coast Bivalve Research Task Force of 16 to 21 members within 90 days of enactment to review bivalve research, identify applied research needs for quahogs (hard clams) and other bivalves, and support sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. The Task Force must submit an interim progress report within one year and a final report within two years, and it is required to establish work groups, including one on quahog research needs in Rhode Island and across the East Coast and one on climate change impacts. The source text was truncated, so the remaining provisions are not summarized here.

items.summary: S. 3301, the Chip Equipment Quality, Usefulness, and Integrity Protection Act of 2025 or Chip EQUIP Act, was introduced by Senator Kelly and reported by Senator Cruz with an amendment and an amendment to the title on November 20, 2026. The bill adds definitions to Section 9901 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 for completed, fully assembled semiconductor manufacturing equipment and ineligible semiconductor manufacturing equipment made, assembled, or refurbished by foreign entities of concern or their subsidiaries or affiliates. It requires Section 9909 funding agreements to prohibit procurement, installation, or use of such equipment for 10 years, subject to waivers and to exceptions for equipment installed or covered by agreements entered before enactment. The amended title reads: A bill to prohibit purchases of certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment from foreign entities of concern or subsidiaries or affiliates of foreign entities of concern, and for other purposes.
items.title: 119 S3301 RS: Chip EQUIP Act

items.summary: S. 3741, the Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act of 2026, as reported with an amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would direct the Secretary of Commerce to issue regulations within one year of enactment requiring covered providers of synthetic nucleic acids and nucleic acid synthesis equipment to implement sequence-of-concern and customer screening protocols. The regulations would establish a conformity assessment system with audits, a process for revoking conformity status, and civil enforcement by the Attorney General with statutory damages of up to $500,000 for individuals and $750,000 for other persons. The text as provided is truncated, so provisions after the biotechnology governance sandbox section are not reflected in this summary.

items.summary: S. 3954, the No Lifeline for Dead People Act, as reported with an amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would prohibit an eligible telecommunications carrier from providing Lifeline service to a consumer unless the National Verifier has been used to verify the consumer's eligibility and the carrier has used the National Lifeline Accountability Database to determine that the service would not violate restrictions on duplicative support. The bill directs the Federal Communications Commission to coordinate with the Treasury Department on the Do Not Pay Initiative to help prevent Lifeline enrollments of deceased individuals and duplicative support. It also requires a Government Accountability Office study within 18 months of enactment on Lifeline program integrity and enrollment barriers, and an annual FCC report to Congress on eligible, enrolled, denied, abandoned, and disenrolled households.
items.title: 119 S3954 RS: No Lifeline for Dead People Act

items.summary: S. 4256, the Airmen Certificate Accessibility Act, as reported with an amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would add subsection (m) to 49 U.S.C. 44703 allowing an individual holding an airman certificate, including a medical certificate, to present it to the FAA Administrator or a designee as a physical certificate or as a digital certificate stored on an electronic device or in a cloud-based system. Digital certificates would be presented under authentication and verification requirements established by the Administrator. The bill directs the FAA Administrator to issue a final rule by November 30, 2028, updating parts 61, 63, 65, 67, and 107 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations, to implement the amendment.
items.title: 119 S4256 RS: Airmen Certificate Accessibility Act

items.summary: S. 5332, the Cooperative Institute Act of 2026, as reported with an amendment by the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, would direct the NOAA Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere to maintain a Cooperative Institute program linking NOAA with eligible non-Federal academic or nonprofit research institutions. items.summary: S. 5663, the Promoting Reproducibility and Oversight of Federal Research Act (PROOF Act), was introduced by Sen. Lummis on September 30, 2026, and reported by Sen. Cruz with an amendment from the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation on November 20, 2026. The bill directs the National Science Foundation Director to make competitive, merit-review awards to institutions of higher education to replicate federally funded research, and specifies the application contents, review criteria, and permitted uses of funds, including stipends for eligible STEM master's students. It requires the Director to submit reports to the Senate Commerce Committee and the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee beginning 18 months after the first award and annually thereafter.

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 724 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 69 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES January 9, 2025 Mr. Schmitt introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation No
items.summary: S. 69, the "Curtailing Online Limitations that Lead Unconstitutionally to Democracy's Erosion Act" or "COLLUDE Act," was introduced by Mr. Schmitt on January 9, 2025, referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, and reported by Mr. Cruz on November 20, 2026, with an amendment striking all after the enacting clause. The bill amends Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 230) to add a burden-of-proof provision for certain actions, to deny Section 230(c) protection to providers that restrict legitimate political speech as a result of certain governmental communications, and to define related terms, with exceptions for legitimate law enforcement and national security purposes. The text also defines "covered provider" as a social media platform with at least $250,000,000 in revenue in the preceding 12 months or at least 10,000,000 global monthly active users for three of the preceding 12 months, makes a "prohibited content action" by such a provider unlawful, and authorizes civil actions by affected information content providers with statutory damages, including the greater of $1,000,000 or three times compensatory damages in specified cases.
items.title: 119 S69 RS: Curtailing Online Limitations that Lead Unconstitutionally to Democracy's Erosion Act
